eva: quick flag — after converting hf/xgen-7b with the new script, streaming responses on staging are cutting off mid-sentence. repro: start stream, it returns a full sentence then stops with no error.

sam: can you paste a minimal stream transcript and the model config you used?

eva: pasted below (sanitized). you can see chunking then an immediate stop token appears twice.
```
STREAM CHUNK 1: "We recommend running the maintenance job at midnight to avoid"
STREAM CHUNK 2: " high contention."
STREAM CHUNK 3: ""  <-- server emitted an EOS token here and closed the stream
TOKEN IDS (final step): [1092, 44, 2034, 2, 2]
model config snippet: {
  "eos_token": "" ,
  "special_tokens": ["", "<pad>"]
}
```

maria: looks like the conversion script appended the HF default `` into added_special_tokens while also keeping eos_token set. that gives us duplicated termination tokens in the tokenizer vocabulary/mapping. in token-id land that becomes consecutive 2,2 which our streaming runtime treats as two separate end events (first closes, second is a no-op) — but we're closing on the first and not flushing partial output properly, causing mid-sentence truncation.

priyanka: interestingly, i only hit this when serving the 4-bit quantized variant. float32 build seemed tolerant (still ugly but continued producing). quantization + token-id remap might change logits for the sentinel token so the model emits eos earlier.

sam: two quick ways to address:
1) conversion fix: coalesce/remove duplicate special tokens during tokenizer conversion and ensure `eos_token_id` points to the canonical token id.
2) runtime safety: treat any EOS as termination but also flush the current buffer instead of closing stream immediately; and ignore repeated eos tokens if they come back-to-back.

maria: proposed conversion patch (pseudo):
```python
# convert_tokenizer.py snippet
if config.get('eos_token') in tokenizer.added_tokens:
    tokenizer.added_tokens.remove(config['eos_token'])
# ensure eos_token_id is set to tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(eos_token)
tokenizer.eos_token_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(config['eos_token'])
```

priyanka: also add a small unit test: generate 200 short prompts and assert no premature EOS before 90% of reference completions. logging: count consecutive eos emissions per sample.

convert-bot: conversion job 4321 finished for hf/xgen-7b-quant4. warnings: duplicated special token '', candidate fix suggested in PR #?

eva: i'll open the PR for the conversion change and add the unit test. i'm leaning to also adding the runtime guard since it's low-risk and prevents similar issues for other models.

sam: agree. runtime guard: when streaming, if an EOS arrives, send final chunk but keep the TCP/websocket open for 100ms to accept any trailing tokens, then close. that avoids dropping trailing tokens that sometimes arrive in same step due to batching.

maria: noted — i'll draft the runtime change and a short benchmark: run 1k streams on staging quant4 vs float32 and measure premature_close rate. include the tokenizer mapping diff in the PR so reviewers can validate.

priyanka: one more gotcha — chat templates that append '\nAssistant:' or similar can create suffixes that the tokenizer maps to separate tokens which may equal EOS depending on the model. we should canonicalize chat templates during conversion: map the assistant prefix to tokens that don't contain implicit eos markers.

sam: filing TODOs:
- eva: PR for tokenizer coalesce + unit tests (ETA today)
- maria: runtime guard PR + microbenchmark (ETA tomorrow)
- priyanka: add chat-template tokenization check to conversion tests

eva: thanks. i'll link the failing example and staging traces in the PR. :thumbsup:
